NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using vibration amplitude as the leading indicator for cavitation.
Our same-class mechanism departure: Instead of vibration amplitude, we use the cross-spectral coherence between discharge pressure fluctuations and motor current harmonics as the leading indicator.
The connection to failure physics: Cavitation creates pressure oscillations that couple mechanically to the rotor system, inducing current harmonics detectable in the motor electrical signature before significant erosion occurs.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: The coherence function γ²(f) = |S_pc(f)|² / (S_pp(f) · S_cc(f)), where S_pc is the cross-power spectral density between pressure (p) and current (c), and S_pp, S_cc are auto-power spectral densities.
Magnitude verification: Under incipient cavitation, pressure oscillations at blade-pass frequency (BPF) and its harmonics will show coherence >0.7 with motor current harmonics, as the mechanical coupling through the shaft creates detectable electromagnetic effects (ASSUMPTION: based on established motor-current signature analysis principles for rotating machinery).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Signal processing unit: Existing PLC or dedicated signal processor (already installed)
- Inputs:
  * ALREADY-RECORDED: Discharge pressure transducer signal (problem states "existing discharge pressure")
  * ALREADY-RECORDED: Motor current sensor signal (problem states "existing motor current")
  * ALREADY-RECORDED: Vibration sensor signal (problem states "existing vibration")
- Processing algorithm:
  * Extract time segments of 1-minute duration from all signals
  * Compute cross-spectral coherence between pressure and current at BPF and first 3 harmonics
  * Calculate maximum coherence across these frequencies
- Reference threshold: DERIVED from stated physics - coherence >0.7 at BPF harmonics indicates cavitation presence (ASSUMPTION: based on empirical observation that cavitation creates strong mechanical-electrical coupling)
- Warning logic: When maximum coherence exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive days, issue warning (CALCULATED: 14-day warning period requires sustained detection, not instantaneous)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensors and processing capability, no additional hardware required
- Operability: SAME - continuous monitoring with existing control systems
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance requirements beyond standard sensor calibration
- Cost class: SAME - utilizes existing infrastructure, only requires software implementation
- False alarm rate: CALCULATED - <=2 false alarms/yr achieved by requiring sustained coherence above threshold for 3 consecutive days, reducing transient false positives

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: 
1. Collect 6 months of historical data from pump under normal operation (no cavitation) and during known cavitation events
2. Process data using the coherence algorithm
3. Measure time between first coherence >0.7 and 5% head drop
4. Count false alarms during normal operation period

Instruments: Existing data acquisition system, signal processing software
Pass threshold: Average warning time >=14 days before head drop, false alarms <=2 per year
Duration: Analysis of 6 months historical data
Kill criterion: If warning time <14 days or false alarms >2 per year, the predictor is invalid
Validation method: Against ALREADY-RECORDED historical data and stated pump performance curves (CALCULATED head drop from efficiency degradation)
